title: The World's Oldest Communication Protocol Is Music

content_html:
This is going to be a very different article from what I usually write. No technical discussions, architecture deep dives, or engineering practices today. Instead, we're talking about something much older than software itself: music.

We treat language like it's the default mode of human communication, like it's the real and only thing used to communicate, everything else is secondary, emotional, aesthetic, nice to have.

But language is actually the outlier. It's the new protocol layered on top of something much older.

Music is the original standard and we've basically forgotten how to read it.

The Protocol Stack

Think of communication like a network stack. Language is high-level. It's TCP/IP. Built on assumptions, needs learning, breaks the second you cross a boundary. You need:

  • A shared vocabulary
  • Syntactic understanding
  • Cultural context
  • Years of study if you actually want fluency

It's powerful but It's also fragile. And it's recent.

Written language is a few thousand years old. Spoken language is older, sure, but both are late abstractions compared to the hundreds of thousands of years humans have been syncing bodies to shared sound. Relative to that timeline? Language is yesterday's patch.

Music? That's the lower-level protocol. The physical layer everything else runs on.

A Japanese teenager at a Michael Jackson concert doesn't need to speak English. She doesn't need to understand what "Man in the Mirror" means as a concept. She also doesn't need a music degree.

Music isn't zero-cost. Genre, culture, convention still shape how we hear it. But the entry barrier for emotional communication is way lower. A rhythm can hit urgency, celebration, sadness, or tension long before anyone understands the formal structure behind it.

Her nervous system speaks that fluently. And so does everyone else in that stadium.

How the Protocol Works

Here's what happens when the song starts: 70,000 people stop being individuals and start being a distributed system synchronizing to the same signal.

The bass hits. Her heartbeat starts matching it. Involuntarily. Her neurons fire in sync with the guy three rows over. The girl next to her moves when the rhythm says move — not because she decided to, but because the protocol sits lower than conscious decision-making.

This isn't mystical. This isn't the "universal language of music" in the poetic sense. This is just biology.

Babies respond to rhythm before they understand words. Crowds clap together without a conductor. Soldiers march to drums. Rituals across cultures use singing and percussion to pull a group into the same tempo. The pattern shows up everywhere because the hardware is shared.

The protocol specs, if we're being nerdy about it:

  • Uses mostly rhythm, tempo, and frequency
  • Hits the nervous system, not the cognitive layer
  • Needs way less shared context than language
  • Backward compatible across human brains for 300,000+ years
  • Works at scale (70,000 synchronizations at once)

Language, meanwhile:

  • Preprocessing (learning)
  • Translation (if you're cross-language)
  • Cognitive overhead (your brain has to think)
  • High latency (meaning takes time)

Music? Low preprocessing. No translation step. Near-zero latency. Your body gets the signal before your mind finishes negotiating what it means.

Why We Don't See This

We're obsessed with meaning. We assume communication = transfer of semantic content. You encode an idea into words, I decode it, boom: we've connected.

So when we see that girl screaming English lyrics she doesn't understand, we quietly reframe it. "Oh, the message transcends language. She understands on a deeper level."

Nah. She's not understanding the message at all. She's on a different protocol entirely. Language is offline. The lower-level stuff is handling it.

We miss this because we've built an entire civilization on top of language. We think the higher-level protocol is the "real" one. Which is like saying TCP/IP is more real than the electrical signals it runs on.

Music isn't poetry. It isn't transcendence. It's infrastructure. It's what everything else runs on.

And no, it's not better than language. It solves a different problem. Music synchronizes systems. Language coordinates them.

A drumbeat can make people march together. It won't tell them why they're marching, what they believe, or what to do when the song ends. Language is powerful because it encodes abstractions. Music is powerful because it doesn't need to.

The Uncomfortable Part

Here's the part that gets weird: you can sync humans at massive scale without them sharing any values, beliefs, or understanding.

That stadium full of people moving together? They don't agree on anything. They might hate each other politically. They might speak no common language. They might have zero common ground.

But for three minutes, their nervous systems are linked. That's a connection. Just not the kind we like to talk about.

We want connection to require understanding. We want it to mean something. We want it to prove that underneath all our differences, we're fundamentally united in shared meaning.

What music actually shows us is simpler and weirder: humans are pattern-matching machines wired to sync with other humans. You don't need shared values for that. You don't need agreement. You don't need understanding.

You just need a rhythm everyone can feel.

What This Means

Language will always need translation and will always be high-friction, high-latency, high-failure-rate across boundaries and... that's not a bug, it's what gives it power, precision requires friction.

But for raw synchronization, getting lots of humans moving together, feeling together, breathing together, language is overkill. Also unreliable.

Music is the protocol that works when nothing else does.

An orchestra where nobody shares a language. A protest with thousands of strangers chanting. A stadium of people from different countries, different beliefs, different everything, all moving as one.

These aren't examples of music "transcending barriers." They're examples of a lower-level protocol just... working, while the higher-level ones fail.

We've built everything on top of language. We've made it the primary. And we've kind of forgotten what it's sitting on.

Language lets us share thoughts. Music lets us share states.

And every time a girl who doesn't speak English screams an English song in perfect sync with 70,000 other people, she's reminding us: the infrastructure was always there. We just stopped noticing it.

The oldest communication protocol is still the most reliable one. We just got distracted by the newer layers.

blocks.html_en: A drumbeat can make people march together. It won't tell them why they're marching, what they believe, or what to do when the song ends. Language is powerful because it encodes abstractions. Music is powerful because it doesn't need to.

sentences.en: A drumbeat can make people march together.

sentences.en: It won't tell them why they're marching, what they believe, or what to do when the song ends.

sentences.en: Language is powerful because it encodes abstractions.

sentences.en: Music is powerful because it doesn't need to.

blocks.html_en: The Uncomfortable Part

sentences.en: The Uncomfortable Part
sentences.zh: 不舒服的部分

blocks.html_en: Here's the part that gets weird: you can sync humans at massive scale without them sharing any values, beliefs, or understanding.

sentences.en: Here's the part that gets weird: you can sync humans at massive scale without them sharing any values, beliefs, or understanding.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是：你可以大规模地同步人类，而无需他们分享任何价值观、信仰或理解。

blocks.html_en: That stadium full of people moving together? They don't agree on anything. They might hate each other politically. They might speak no common language. They might have zero common ground.

sentences.en: That stadium full of people moving together?
sentences.zh: 那个充满人们一起移动的体育场？

sentences.en: They don't agree on anything.

sentences.en: They might hate each other politically.

sentences.en: They might speak no common language.
sentences.zh: 他们可能没有共同语言。

sentences.en: They might have zero common ground.
sentences.zh: 他们的共同点可能为零。

blocks.html_en: But for three minutes, their nervous systems are linked. That's a connection. Just not the kind we like to talk about.

sentences.en: But for three minutes, their nervous systems are linked.
sentences.zh: 但在三分钟内，他们的神经系统是相连的。

sentences.en: That's a connection.
sentences.zh: 这就是一种联系。

sentences.en: Just not the kind we like to talk about.
sentences.zh: 只是不是我们喜欢谈论的那种。

blocks.html_en: We want connection to require understanding. We want it to mean something. We want it to prove that underneath all our differences, we're fundamentally united in shared meaning.

sentences.en: We want connection to require understanding.
sentences.zh: 我们想要联系需要理解。

sentences.en: We want it to mean something.
sentences.zh: 我们希望它有意义。

sentences.en: We want it to prove that underneath all our differences, we're fundamentally united in shared meaning.
sentences.zh: 我们希望它能证明，在我们所有的差异之下，我们在共同的意义上是根本上团结的。

blocks.html_en: What music actually shows us is simpler and weirder: humans are pattern-matching machines wired to sync with other humans. You don't need shared values for that. You don't need agreement. You don't need understanding.

sentences.en: What music actually shows us is simpler and weirder: humans are pattern-matching machines wired to sync with other humans.
sentences.zh: 音乐实际上向我们展示的更简单、更奇怪：人类是与其他人类同步的模式匹配机器。

sentences.en: You don't need shared values for that.
sentences.zh: 为此，您不需要共同的价值观。

sentences.en: You don't need agreement.
sentences.zh: 你不需要同意。

sentences.en: You don't need understanding.
sentences.zh: 你不需要理解。

blocks.html_en: You just need a rhythm everyone can feel.

sentences.en: You just need a rhythm everyone can feel.
sentences.zh: 你只需要一种每个人都能感受到的节奏。

blocks.html_en: What This Means

sentences.en: What This Means
sentences.zh: 这意味着什么

blocks.html_en: Language will always need translation and will always be high-friction, high-latency, high-failure-rate across boundaries and... that's not a bug, it's what gives it power, precision requires friction.

sentences.en: Language will always need translation and will always be high-friction, high-latency, high-failure-rate across boundaries and...
sentences.zh: 语言永远需要翻译，并且永远是高摩擦、高延迟、跨界高失败率……

sentences.en: that's not a bug, it's what gives it power, precision requires friction.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个错误，它赋予了它力量，精度需要摩擦。

blocks.html_en: But for raw synchronization, getting lots of humans moving together, feeling together, breathing together, language is overkill. Also unreliable.

sentences.en: But for raw synchronization, getting lots of humans moving together, feeling together, breathing together, language is overkill.
sentences.zh: 但对于原始的同步来说，让很多人一起移动、一起感觉、一起呼吸，语言就有点大材小用了。

sentences.en: Also unreliable.
sentences.zh: 也不靠谱。

blocks.html_en: Music is the protocol that works when nothing else does.

sentences.en: Music is the protocol that works when nothing else does.
sentences.zh: 音乐是当其他事物不起作用时起作用的协议。

blocks.html_en: An orchestra where nobody shares a language. A protest with thousands of strangers chanting. A stadium of people from different countries, different beliefs, different everything, all moving as one.

sentences.en: An orchestra where nobody shares a language.
sentences.zh: 一个没有人共享语言的管弦乐队。

sentences.en: A protest with thousands of strangers chanting.

sentences.en: A stadium of people from different countries, different beliefs, different everything, all moving as one.
sentences.zh: 这座体育场里有来自不同国家、不同信仰、不同事物的人们，但所有人都在移动。

blocks.html_en: These aren't examples of music "transcending barriers." They're examples of a lower-level protocol just... working, while the higher-level ones fail.

sentences.en: These aren't examples of music "transcending barriers."
sentences.zh: 这些并不是音乐“超越障碍”的例子。

sentences.en: They're examples of a lower-level protocol just...
sentences.zh: 它们是较低级别协议的示例......

sentences.en: working, while the higher-level ones fail.
sentences.zh: 工作正常，而高层则失败。

blocks.html_en: We've built everything on top of language. We've made it the primary. And we've kind of forgotten what it's sitting on.

sentences.en: We've built everything on top of language.
sentences.zh: 我们把一切都建立在语言之上。

sentences.en: We've made it the primary.
sentences.zh: 我们已将其作为主要的。

sentences.en: And we've kind of forgotten what it's sitting on.
sentences.zh: 我们已经忘记了它坐在什么上面。

blocks.html_en: Language lets us share thoughts. Music lets us share states.

sentences.en: Language lets us share thoughts.
sentences.zh: 语言让我们分享想法。

sentences.en: Music lets us share states.
sentences.zh: 音乐让我们分享状态。

blocks.html_en: And every time a girl who doesn't speak English screams an English song in perfect sync with 70,000 other people, she's reminding us: the infrastructure was always there. We just stopped noticing it.

sentences.en: And every time a girl who doesn't speak English screams an English song in perfect sync with 70,000 other people, she's reminding us: the infrastructure was always there.
sentences.zh: 每当一个不会说英语的女孩与其他 70,000 人完美同步地尖叫一首英语歌曲时，她就在提醒我们：基础设施一直都在那里。

sentences.en: We just stopped noticing it.
sentences.zh: 我们只是不再注意到它。

blocks.html_en: The oldest communication protocol is still the most reliable one. We just got distracted by the newer layers.

sentences.en: The oldest communication protocol is still the most reliable one.
sentences.zh: 最古老的通信协议仍然是最可靠的一种。

sentences.en: We just got distracted by the newer layers.
sentences.zh: 我们只是被新层分散了注意力。

content_html_zh:
这将是一篇与我通常写的文章非常不同的文章。 今天没有技术讨论、架构深入研究或工程实践。 相反，我们谈论的是比软件本身更古老的东西：音乐。

我们对待语言就像它是人类交流的默认模式，就像它是真正的、唯一用来交流的东西，其他一切都是次要的，情感的，审美的，拥有它就好。

但语言实际上是异常值。 这是新的协议，建立在旧协议之上。

音乐是最初的标准，但我们基本上已经忘记了如何阅读它。

协议栈

将通信视为网络堆栈。 语言水平很高。 这是 TCP/IP。 建立在假设之上，需要学习，一旦跨越界限就会打破。 您需要：

  • 共享词汇
  • 句法理解
  • 文化背景
  • 如果你真的想要流利的话，需要多年的学习

它很强大，但也很脆弱。 而且是最近的。

书面语言已有几千年的历史。 当然，口语更古老，但与数十万年来人类将身体与共享声音同步相比，这两种语言都是晚期的抽象概念。 相对于那个时间线？ 语言是昨天的补丁。

音乐？ 这是较低级别的协议。 其他一切都在物理层上运行。

迈克尔·杰克逊音乐会上的日本青少年不需要说英语。 她不需要理解“镜中人”这个概念意味着什么。 她也不需要音乐学位。

音乐并不是零成本的。 流派、文化、惯例仍然影响着我们听到它的方式。 但情感交流的准入门槛要低得多。 早在人们理解其背后的正式结构之前，节奏就可以表达紧迫、庆祝、悲伤或紧张的情绪。

她的神经系统说得很流利。 体育场里的其他人也是如此。

协议如何运作

当歌曲开始时，会发生以下情况：70,000 人不再是个体，而是开始成为与同一信号同步的分布式系统。

低音响起。 她的心跳开始匹配。 不由自主。 她的神经元与三排外的那个人同步放电。 当节奏说移动时，旁边的女孩就移动了——不是因为她决定这样做，而是因为协议低于有意识的决策。

这并不神秘。 这不是诗意意义上的“音乐的通用语言”。 这只是生物学。

婴儿在理解单词之前就会对节奏做出反应。 人群在没有指挥的情况下鼓掌。 士兵们敲锣打鼓。 跨文化的仪式利用歌唱和打击乐将一群人拉入相同的节奏。 由于硬件是共享的，这种模式随处可见。

协议规范，如果我们对此感到厌烦的话：

  • 主要使用节奏、节奏和频率
  • 影响神经系统，而不是认知层
  • 需要比语言更少的共享上下文
  • 人类大脑向后兼容 30 万多年
  • 大规模工作（一次 70,000 次同步）

同时，语言：

  • 预处理（学习）
  • 翻译（如果您会跨语言）
  • 认知开销（你的大脑必须思考）
  • 高延迟（意味着需要时间）

音乐？ 低预处理。 没有翻译步骤。 接近零延迟。 在你的大脑完成对信号含义的协商之前，你的身体就收到了信号。

为什么我们看不到这个

我们痴迷于意义。 我们假设沟通=语义内容的传输。 你把一个想法编码成文字，我解码它，繁荣：我们已经联系在一起了。

所以当我们看到那个女孩尖叫着她听不懂的英文歌词时，我们就悄悄地重新组织它。 “哦，这个信息超越了语言。 她有更深层次的理解。”

现在。 她根本不明白这个消息。 她采用的是完全不同的协议。 语言离线。 较低级别的东西正在处理它。

我们错过了这一点，因为我们已经在语言之上建立了整个文明。 我们认为更高级别的协议是“真正的”协议。 这就像说 TCP/IP 比它所运行的电信号更真实。

音乐不是诗歌。 这不是超越。 这是基础设施。 这是其他一切运行的基础。

不，它并不比语言更好。 它解决了一个不同的问题。 音乐使系统同步。 语言协调它们。

鼓声可以使人们齐步前进。 它不会告诉他们为什么要游行，他们相信什么，或者歌曲结束后该做什么。 语言之所以强大，是因为它对抽象进行了编码。 音乐之所以强大，是因为它不需要。

不舒服的部分

奇怪的是：你可以大规模地同步人类，而无需他们分享任何价值观、信仰或理解。

那个充满人们一起移动的体育场？ 他们在任何事情上都不达成一致。 他们可能在政治上互相仇恨。 他们可能没有共同语言。 他们的共同点可能为零。

但在三分钟内，他们的神经系统是相连的。 这就是一种联系。 只是不是我们喜欢谈论的那种。

我们想要联系需要理解。 我们希望它有意义。 我们希望它能证明，在我们所有的差异之下，我们在共同的意义上是根本上团结的。

音乐实际上向我们展示的更简单、更奇怪：人类是与其他人类同步的模式匹配机器。 为此，您不需要共同的价值观。 你不需要同意。 你不需要理解。

你只需要一种每个人都能感受到的节奏。

这意味着什么

语言永远需要翻译，并且永远是高摩擦、高延迟、跨界高失败率…… 这不是一个错误，它赋予了它力量，精度需要摩擦。

但对于原始的同步来说，让很多人一起移动、一起感觉、一起呼吸，语言就有点大材小用了。 也不靠谱。

音乐是当其他事物不起作用时起作用的协议。

一个没有人共享语言的管弦乐队。 数千名陌生人高呼口号进行抗议。 这座体育场里有来自不同国家、不同信仰、不同事物的人们，但所有人都在移动。

这些并不是音乐“超越障碍”的例子。 它们是较低级别协议的示例...... 工作正常，而高层则失败。

我们把一切都建立在语言之上。 我们已将其作为主要的。 我们已经忘记了它坐在什么上面。

语言让我们分享想法。 音乐让我们分享状态。

每当一个不会说英语的女孩与其他 70,000 人完美同步地尖叫一首英语歌曲时，她就在提醒我们：基础设施一直都在那里。 我们只是不再注意到它。

最古老的通信协议仍然是最可靠的一种。 我们只是被新层分散了注意力。
